notify.success_note: You are on the list. Watch your inbox.

steps.title: The shoulder
steps.body: The reed is opened at a long shallow angle so the ink has somewhere to sit. Cut it short and the pen runs dry mid-letter.

steps.title: The slit
steps.body: One press splits the nib down the centre. It has to stop exactly where the shoulder ends, or the two halves will spread under pressure.

steps.title: The qatt
steps.body: The tip is trimmed against the qat'ah at the angle your script needs — flat for thuluth, oblique for nastaliq. This is the cut you cannot take back.

items.question: Can I order before the shop opens?
items.answer: No. Lot One is cut in a single run and every piece goes to the list in the order names came in. Adding your name is the whole queue.

items.question: Do you cut for left hands?
items.answer: Yes. Say so when you order and the qatt is reversed. There is no extra charge and no extra wait.

items.question: How long does a reed pen last?
items.answer: A season of daily practice, then it wants re-cutting. We send a qat'ah with every pen and instructions for the second cut.

items.question: Do you ship outside the country?
items.answer: Not for Lot One. Ink is a problem at customs and we would rather solve it properly than lose your parcel.
